name: Bezaleel and Aholiab
charge: Making all that the Lord commanded, and no more; and teaching others to do it
summary: The Lord called Bezaleel of Judah by name and filled him with the spirit of God in wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all manner of workmanship, gave him Aholiab of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted. God sets every member in the body as it pleases him. They made every piece to the pattern and taught their brethren, and Moses looked upon all the work and blessed them.
offenseFull: The Lord told Moses that he had called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and had filled him with the spirit of God in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works in gold, in silver and in brass, in cutting of stones and in carving of timber; and that he had given him Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and had put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make everything he had commanded (Exodus 31:1-6). The first men in scripture said to be filled with the spirit of God were filled for the work of their hands. Bezaleel most likely never thought God had given him anything; in his own mind he was just good at something. The talent was given for that purpose, so that the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the garments and the vessels could be made.

The Most High still works the same way. He sets the members, every one of them, in the body as it has pleased him, and there are diversities of operations but the same God working all in all, and the body is not one member but many (1 Corinthians 12:6-11, 14, 18). Carpenters, builders, painters, cooks and craftsmen come into the congregation, and the Lord sends the souls in so that the work gets done; a school goes from a folding table with a cloth on it to a built stage because the Lord brought builders in. But no man appoints himself, and no man sits on his hands or on somebody else’s gift.

Everyone whose heart stirred him up and whose spirit made him willing brought the Lord’s offering, both men and women, and all the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands (Exodus 35:21-26). The Lord had put it in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab (Exodus 35:34): the two men the Most High dealt with in workmanship trained their brethren how to do it, so Israel put its talents together and built. They worked to the pattern and added nothing, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses (Exodus 39:42).
judgmentFull: Moses looked upon all the work, and they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them (Exodus 39:43). The breastplate carried four rows of stones, twelve according to the names of the children of Israel, every one with his name like the engravings of a signet, and the shoulders of the ephod carried the same for a memorial: when the priest stepped on the scene you already knew what nation he was, because nationality mattered to the Lord and he took it seriously. The bells and the pomegranates went upon the hem of the robe round about, and the account keeps saying round about. The plate of the holy crown was of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD (Exodus 39:8-14, 24-26, 30). Our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real gold; that is the heritage.

Then the cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle they had made (Exodus 40:34). That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and afterward the house Solomon built, outshined anything the world had seen. Their skill was taught out and not held privately, and in the kingdom, though the sons of strangers shall build up our walls, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done (Isaiah 60:10). Every case in Leviticus and Numbers takes place inside or around what these men built.

text.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:
And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,
To devise cunning works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
And in cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of timber, to work in all manner of workmanship.

And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee;
And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.
But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit;
To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit;
To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues:
But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.
For the body is not one member, but many.
But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

And they came, every one whose heart stirred him up, and every one whom his spirit made willing, and they brought the Lord’s offering to the work of the tabernacle of the congregation, and for all his service, and for the holy garments.

And they came, both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, and brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold: and every man that offered offered an offering of gold unto the Lord.
And every man, with whom was found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, and red skins of rams, and badgers’ skins, brought them.
Every one that did offer an offering of silver and brass brought the Lord’s offering: and every man, with whom was found shittim wood for any work of the service, brought it.
And all the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands, and brought that which they had spun, both of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine linen.
And all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats’ hair.
And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
And he made the breastplate of cunning work, like the work of the ephod; of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
It was foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span was the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, being doubled.
And they set in it four rows of stones: the first row was a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this was the first row.
And the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
And the third row, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: they were inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings.
And the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, according to the twelve tribes.
And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined linen.
And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, round about between the pomegranates;
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister in; as the Lord commanded Moses.
And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like to the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.
And Moses said unto the children of Israel, See, the Lord hath called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship;
And to devise curious works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
And in the cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of wood, to make any manner of cunning work.
And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of work, of the engraver, and of the cunning workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of them that do any work, and of those that devise cunning work.
According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined linen.
And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, round about between the pomegranates;
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister in; as the Lord commanded Moses.
And they made coats of fine linen of woven work for Aaron, and for his sons,
And a mitre of fine linen, and goodly bonnets of fine linen, and linen breeches of fine twined linen,
And a girdle of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, of needlework; as the Lord commanded Moses.
And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like to the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
